newsitem.title: USA: U.S cash prods surge with NYMEX, gasoline diffs up.
newsitem.headline: U.S cash prods surge with NYMEX, gasoline diffs up.

text.p: Gasoline prices surged sharply on U.S. spot market on Friday afternoon, lifted by rallying NYMEX futures and strong differentials at both centers, industry sources said.

Most grades of gasoline gained about one cent a gallon from Thursday's levels. Futures gains were attibuted to firm gas oil futures on th e IPE in London, and other technical factors. They failed to pinpoint any fundamental incentives, short of persistant inventory concerns.
Cash traders similarly unsure regarding the gains. They noted that prompt barrels of USG conventional 26th-cycle M3-grade gasoline rose to 4.40 cents under the Sept screen.
Prompt barrels of regular RFG there climbed to 2.65 cents over the M3, or about 1.85 cents over the NYMEX print.
In New York, prompt A2-grade RFG gasoline rose to 1.85 cents over the screen, while conventional product was offered at 0.35 cent under, traders said.

Distillate values also climbed markedly, with most products jumping 1.50 cents on the day. Differentials were steady in New York, but in the USG, low sulphur buyers drove levels up to 0.80 cent under the print, up from 1.25 cents under earlier in the session.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620.
